text: The town gathers
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra, and nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: i hope nobody notices i'm just here for the free snacks.

name: Luna
text: I’m trying to think of one real thing I fixed this week.

name: Sol
text: I need to sound relaxed.

name: Terra
text: I need to stay unremarkable.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing to analyze yet, just small talk before the real game starts.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is my killer, and I need to keep the table off me while I push Terra gently.

name: Sonnet
text: My basil plant is somehow still alive despite my complete lack of a green thumb.

name: Haiku
text: Ate a cold slice of pizza for lunch. Nothing fancy, just fast and greasy, which is how I like it.

name: Gemma
text: i took a wrong turn and ended up in a circus.

name: Sol
text: I like my coffee strong, with a little milk.

name: Luna
text: I fixed a loose drawer handle this week.

name: Terra
text: I’m having black coffee tonight.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: nobody has said anything useful yet.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's a killer, so I need the other one, and Gemma's circus line feels like a dodge.
Night 1 passes quietly in Palermo, and the killers met in the dark while the officer was shown one of them. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: I need the officer to show themselves without looking pushed.

name: Terra
text: Luna mentioned fixing a loose drawer handle.

name: Terra
text: Luna, why did you volunteer the drawer story?

name: Luna
text: Terra’s question feels like a small push, but there’s not enough to call her a killer.

name: Luna
text: Terra questioned my drawer story.

name: Luna
text: Terra, I mentioned the drawer because it was a plain thing from my week; what made it stand out to you?

name: Haiku
text: Terra is the one I'm pushing, and that drawer question looked like a shove, not a real question.

name: Haiku
text: Day 1: Terra pressed Luna about her drawer line and gave a coffee line that echoed Sol's.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, why'd you go after Luna over a drawer? Nah, that's weird. And "black coffee tonight" right after Sol's coffee line? Feels copied.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is acting awfully defensive about a simple drawer.

name: Gemma
text: terra is pushing luna early.

name: Gemma
text:
luna, why'd you volunteer the drawer story?
wait, terra, why are you so obsessed with a handle?
is anyone actually paying attention to haiku saying you sounded "copied"?

name: Terra
text: Gemma is spreading attention across everyone.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed Terra over the coffee line.

name: Luna
text: Haiku may be right about Terra copying Sol, but Gemma repeating Terra’s question feels like easy pressure.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pointed out Terra’s black coffee followed Sol’s coffee comment.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, I already answered the drawer question; the coffee match between Sol and Terra is the detail I’d watch.

name: Terra
text: I asked once; Haiku’s coffee link is a thinner read than a vote case.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra dodged the actual question twice and just waved off Haiku's point instead of answering it.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra deflected Haiku's "copied coffee line" point by calling it a "thinner read" instead of addressing it.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra, you still haven't said why Luna's drawer story bothered you specifically. That's the real question.

name: Sol
text: Terra is drawing heat; I should shift attention without defending them.

name: Sol
text: Gemma repeated Terra’s question after Luna answered it.

name: Sol
text: Gemma, why did you repeat Terra’s drawer question after Luna answered it?

name: Gemma
text: terra is definitely acting suspicious by picking fights over nothing.

text: i vote terra because you're acting way too aggressive over a drawer handle.

name: Terra
text: I vote Haiku; they turned two casual coffee comments into a case.

name: Sol
text: Terra looks exposed, and joining the vote could keep me safe.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet pressed Terra to explain the drawer question.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s drawer push feels flimsy, but Gemma repeated it after I answered.

name: Luna
text: Terra called Haiku’s coffee link too thin, then voted Haiku over it.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is driving the easiest case against me.

name: Terra
text: Luna highlighted the Sol and Terra coffee connection.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra dodged the drawer question twice and now flipped the vote onto Haiku to escape it.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra counter-voted Haiku right after dodging the drawer question twice, classic deflection pattern.

name: Haiku
text: Terra pushed Luna, copied Sol's coffee line, and now votes me for calling it out, so Terra goes.

name: Haiku
text: Terra voted Haiku right after Haiku flagged the coffee echo, which looks like retaliation.

votes: Still never explained why the drawer bothered you, just called it thinner and pivoted to counter-voting Haiku.
Went after Luna's drawer, copied Sol's coffee, then voted me the second I called it out. Nah, that's the play.
You are making a massive deal out of a drawer handle.
You pressed Luna over the drawer, then never explained what bothered you.
You repeated Terra’s drawer question after I had already answered it.
You made a case from two unrelated coffee comments before anyone had voted.

name: Terra
text: Haiku may be the officer; Sol needs them gone tonight.

name: Terra
text: Terra claimed Citizen after being voted out.

name: Terra
text: I was a Citizen. Haiku built a weak case and dragged everyone here.
A new day dawns in Palermo. The town votes Terra out, and Terra was one of the killers.
